about.description:
Spec42 is local-first tooling for SysML v2 and KerML. The same analysis engine
backs the language server (LSP over stdio, used by the VS Code and Zed
extensions) and the `spec42` command line interface, so editor feedback and CI
validation agree.

This package provides the `spec42` executable — `spec42 lsp` for editor
integration, `spec42 check` for validation with text, JSON, SARIF, or JUnit
output, `spec42 bundle` and `spec42 unbundle` for building and unpacking KerML
Project Archive (KPAR) files, plus model summary and diagram export subcommands.

The OMG SysML v2 standard library and the Elan8 domain and method libraries are
embedded in the binary, so no network access is required at run time. The VS Code
and Zed extensions are not part of this package; install them from their
respective marketplaces and point them at this `spec42` binary.
about.summary: SysML v2 and KerML language server, CLI, and model validator

raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  version: "0.51.0"
  # The bundled library versions are pinned by the source tree, not chosen here:
  #   stdlib_version -> config/standard-library.json  (version + repo + contentPath, and
  #                                                    since 0.51.0 a `projects` list that
  #                                                    the ten stdlib sources below mirror)
  #   domain_version -> config/libraries/domain.json  (version + artifact)
  #   method_version -> config/libraries/method.json  (version + artifact)
  # crates/workspace/build.rs refuses to build with the default `embed-stdlib` /
  # `embed-kpar-libraries` features unless it finds these archives, so they have to be
  # fetched as recipe sources rather than by upstream's scripts/fetch-*.sh (which clone
  # and curl at build time). Re-check the three config files on every version bump.
  stdlib_version: "2026-04"
  domain_version: "0.3.0"
  method_version: "0.2.0"
  # Upstream tags the OMG release rather than attaching archives to it, and the whole
  # repository tarball is ~96 MB for ~250 kB of KPAR archives, so the individual files
  # are fetched from the tag instead.
  stdlib_url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Systems-Modeling/SysML-v2-Release/${{ stdlib_version }}/sysml.library.kpar
  # Default cache layout that crates/workspace/build.rs probes, relative to the workspace
  # root: `.cache/sysml-stdlib-kpar-<version>/*.kpar` and `.cache/<artifact>.kpar`.
  stdlib_dir: .cache/sysml-stdlib-kpar-${{ stdlib_version }}

package:
  name: spec42
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://github.com/elan8/spec42/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: b920918faa2317193f9bfc246e51acf273790564967d06c51863104adcb2d347

  # OMG SysML v2 / KerML standard library, embedded into the binary by the `embed-stdlib`
  # feature. The library versions below are those shipped in the ${{ stdlib_version }} release
  # and are independent of the release date; they change when OMG revises a library.
  - url: ${{ stdlib_url }}/Kernel_Data_Type_Library-1.0.0.kpar
    sha256: 9f2bf2ebf72c6cb9f4a53999afe5e382bf65acfbc0f455ce2ca5ffe1e621326d
    target_directory: ${{ stdlib_dir }}
  - url: ${{ stdlib_url }}/Kernel_Function_Library-1.0.0.kpar
    sha256: 05c57ed433073fde16f2a52bdbbe6ac099ce52520bfdf41893f7b49866aa24f4
    target_directory: ${{ stdlib_dir }}
  - url: ${{ stdlib_url }}/Kernel_Semantic_Library-1.0.0.kpar
    sha256: e741ff98b689b6596da5078ec1693928a94d2f8a090a476e1f3e7a7f5d0abb84
    target_directory: ${{ stdlib_dir }}
  - url: ${{ stdlib_url }}/SysML_Analysis_Library-2.0.0.kpar
    sha256: aa9b52c8e5954fefd8957400aa5a8a748d13e0bc227f5c1f7c6c5cc852e086d9
    target_directory: ${{ stdlib_dir }}
  - url: ${{ stdlib_url }}/SysML_Cause_and_Effect_Library-2.0.0.kpar
    sha256: 022c3cc4a99aad9ce0d98a7c7c6de7eb6c4f6a2020cf85cb21c250fb5c737b64
    target_directory: ${{ stdlib_dir }}
  - url: ${{ stdlib_url }}/SysML_Geometry_Library-2.0.0.kpar
    sha256: 96b3f9de7d6e8be1638aa5e68386b389bf9f9030b57c8febcbfb253eb12dacac
    target_directory: ${{ stdlib_dir }}
  - url: ${{ stdlib_url }}/SysML_Metadata_Library-2.0.0.kpar
    sha256: 428cebf6efb4ace8320a1bb660369988b4d8634997b054dd1ffca3da5568c4c5
    target_directory: ${{ stdlib_dir }}
  - url: ${{ stdlib_url }}/SysML_Quantities_and_Units_Library-2.0.0.kpar
    sha256: 2da5cc70598fd6fcfe2e3e9503942a48da2120252fffa0b9ff012a601f9a3acb
    target_directory: ${{ stdlib_dir }}
  - url: ${{ stdlib_url }}/SysML_Requirement_Derivation_Library-2.0.0.kpar
    sha256: ce0e0246d47b613e5a1a39ed253071f89d3c69035afc5282076b381f1a633238
    target_directory: ${{ stdlib_dir }}
  - url: ${{ stdlib_url }}/SysML_Systems_Library-2.0.0.kpar
    sha256: 7a8ea690b110466f50c52b8c594b9815a331377baebc2794958203b264d01bac
    target_directory: ${{ stdlib_dir }}

  # Licence covering the embedded standard library above. It also covers the ELK.js
  # assets that crates/server `include_str!`s into the binary, which are EPL-2.0 too and
  # ship without a licence file of their own in the spec42 tree.
  # Note that spec42's own THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md describes the standard library as
  # "GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0 / related notices", which does not match the
  # pinned release: the LICENSE fetched here is plain EPL-2.0 (its Exhibit A secondary
  # licence placeholder is left unfilled), and the upstream README states that all
  # included KerML and SysML v2 models are licensed under EPL v2.0.
  - url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Systems-Modeling/SysML-v2-Release/${{ stdlib_version }}/LICENSE
    sha256: 0becf16567beb77fa252b7664631dd177c8f9a1889e48995b45379c7130e5303
    file_name: LICENSE.sysml-v2-release-EPL-2.0

  # Elan8 domain and method libraries, embedded by the `embed-kpar-libraries` feature.
  # These are prebuilt release assets, so build.rs copies them instead of packing them.
  - url: https://github.com/elan8/sysml-domain-libraries/releases/download/v${{ domain_version }}/elan8-domain-libraries-${{ domain_version }}.kpar
    sha256: af457fb32a158a38c0a7513a0bf2397b99659bafcb8e3e5d735f491e8de09735
    target_directory: .cache
  - url: https://github.com/elan8/mbse-methodology/releases/download/v${{ method_version }}/elan8-method-libraries-${{ method_version }}.kpar
    sha256: 31b9a04d53f4ebd7e4a48f1ee1f45b25586d9bebb536cc807915b6e6442882c9
    target_directory: .cache

build:
  number: 0

requirements:
  build:
    # A C toolchain is needed because cc drives the final link of the Rust binaries.
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    - ${{ compiler('rust') }}
    # The crate graph is pure Rust, so the vendored dependency licences have to be
    # collected into a single file for the package.
    - cargo-bundle-licenses

tests:
  - package_contents:
      bin:
        - spec42

  - script:
      - spec42 --version
      - spec42 --help
      - spec42 lsp --help
      - spec42 check --help
      # KPAR archives are created and unpacked through these subcommands. Up to 0.50.0
      # the packing half was a second binary, `kpar-pack` from crates/kpar; 0.51.0 made
      # that crate a library only (it no longer even depends on clap), so the archive
      # commands exist solely as part of `spec42`.
      - spec42 bundle --help
      - spec42 unbundle --help

  # These resolve and materialise the libraries baked in at build time, so they fail if
  # the embedded stdlib or KPAR bundles did not make it into the binary.
  #
  # Unix only. Every spec42 subcommand that touches the environment starts with an
  # unconditional `project_dirs()?` (crates/server/src/environment.rs), which is
  # `ProjectDirs::from` from directories 5. On Windows that resolves the roaming AppData
  # known folder through SHGetKnownFolderPath, which fails on a build agent running
  # without a loaded user profile — "Could not determine a user config directory for
  # spec42." Because that call precedes the SPEC42_CONFIG_DIR / SPEC42_DATA_DIR overrides
  # rather than falling back to them, no environment variable can make it succeed here.
  # It resolves normally for an interactive Windows user, so this is a limitation of the
  # test sandbox, not of the package.
  - if: unix
    then:
      script:
        - spec42 stdlib status
        - spec42 libraries status

about:
  homepage: https://elan8.github.io/spec42/
  summary: SysML v2 and KerML language server, CLI, and model validator
  description: |
    Spec42 is local-first tooling for SysML v2 and KerML. The same analysis engine
    backs the language server (LSP over stdio, used by the VS Code and Zed
    extensions) and the `spec42` command line interface, so editor feedback and CI
    validation agree.

    This package provides the `spec42` executable — `spec42 lsp` for editor
    integration, `spec42 check` for validation with text, JSON, SARIF, or JUnit
    output, `spec42 bundle` and `spec42 unbundle` for building and unpacking KerML
    Project Archive (KPAR) files, plus model summary and diagram export subcommands.

    The OMG SysML v2 standard library and the Elan8 domain and method libraries are
    embedded in the binary, so no network access is required at run time. The VS Code
    and Zed extensions are not part of this package; install them from their
    respective marketplaces and point them at this `spec42` binary.
  # The binary is not just spec42's own MIT code: the build embeds the OMG SysML v2 /
  # KerML standard library and `include_str!`s the vendored ELK.js assets, both EPL-2.0.
  # The Elan8 domain and method libraries are also embedded and are MIT, so they need no
  # separate term in the expression.
  license: MIT AND EPL-2.0
  license_file:
    # spec42's own MIT licence.
    - LICENSE
    # Upstream's summary of what it vendors and embeds.
    - THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
    # Licences of every statically linked Rust crate, generated by cargo-bundle-licenses.
    - THIRDPARTY.yml
    # EPL-2.0, covering the embedded standard library and the vendored ELK.js assets.
    - LICENSE.sysml-v2-release-EPL-2.0
    # The Elan8 domain and method libraries are embedded from release archives whose
    # source repositories carry no licence file; this records the MIT grant that the
    # archives themselves declare.
    - LICENSE.elan8-libraries.md
  documentation: https://elan8.github.io/spec42/
  repository: https://github.com/elan8/spec42

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - phreed
